full_text:
Several of the most popular stats used to evaluate QBs in fantasy football are completely worthless. But others — and probably not the ones you think — are overwhelmingly valuable.

In this article, I’ll show you which stats belong in which bucket, then use that knowledge to highlight five of my favorite QB values for 2026 fantasy football. (Feel free to scroll down to that part if the fantasy takes are all you’re here for!)

I tested almost every stat in the [*Fantasy Points Data Suite*](https://data.fantasypoints.com/) (along with a handful we haven’t even added yet!) for how well it predicts *next year’s* fantasy points per game (FPG). Results for the QB position are in the graphic below, sorted from highest to lowest correlation coefficient.

![](STATIC_ASSET_URI/photos/d3188d228fc8bbca9abe6059cdeaf2b85e9c7086/eae1f4e560d90297cc1d69bdc2d78eeb073cf8a9)

Metrics with stronger correlations are the best at predicting future fantasy scoring in isolation. As an obvious example to illustrate, “Josh Allen led all QBs in rushing attempts in 2025, so it’s likely he’ll lead the position in FPG in 2026” *__is__* a statement supported by the above analysis. Rushing attempts display a 0.576 correlation coefficient with next-season FPG, the strongest relationship on the list.

In contrast, “Drake Maye led all QBs in Completion %, so it’s likely he’ll lead the position in FPG in 2026” *__is not__* supported by the analysis above. Completion % has just a 0.154 correlation coefficient with next-season FPG, ranking closer to the bottom of the list.

That’s not to say that Completion % — or Pressure Rate, or Average Time to Throw, or Off-Target Throw Rate, or any of the other stats ranking near the bottom — can’t tell you *anything*. It’s just that they measure much narrower aspects of QB play and team environment that aren’t useful *in isolation* for predicting fantasy scoring, mostly because we can’t know in which direction they’ll move without other context.

For example, if you can demonstrate that a QB’s pressure rate will *decrease* in 2026 because of offensive line improvements, that could be part of a great argument in his favor! Every stat is just a tool in our tool belt.

 QB fantasy points per dropback league-wide, since 2021... When pressured within 2.5 seconds: 0.36 When pressured after 2.5 seconds: 0.40 When not pressured at all: 0.45 A potential 25% increase in fantasy scoring just from not facing quick pressure - @FantasyPtsData — Ryan Heath (@RyanJ_Heath) June 4, 2026 

{{CTA|DataSuite|omit=\[role\_uJb30OfZpu4pFfS7VQEq\]}}

How To Think About QB Metrics
-----------------------------

While there are tons of individual stats I tested in the graphic above, we can broadly group them into a few categories, to which I’ll refer throughout my player write-ups below. Going in order of how predictive they are:

__1A.__ __Rushing volume and production__ — including rush attempts, rushing yards, scrambles, designed carry share, and any of their per-game variations. This shouldn’t be a surprise; we’ve known for years that the “[Konami Code](https://www.fantasypoints.com/nfl/articles/season/2021/konami-code-revisited-mobile-qb-revolution#/)” (originally surfaced by Rich Hribar) is massively important for fantasy QBs. Seriously, rushing is insanely important, as Jacob Gibbs pointed out using an earlier version of this analysis:

 https://t.co/EjajtaMlGL pic.twitter.com/sDtCBibR3S — Jacob Gibbs (@jagibbs_23) June 2, 2026 

In fact, just to make the rest of our analysis clearer, here’s a version of the graphic with all rushing-only stats removed.

![](STATIC_ASSET_URI/photos/d3188d228fc8bbca9abe6059cdeaf2b85e9c7086/35435f14ae12f78ff811fe6e1674d3186f29f202)

__1B. Prior fantasy sc____oring__ — including FPG, fantasy points per opportunity (FP/OPP), fantasy points per dropback (FP/DB), and other variations. Intuitively, a QB having previously put together a big fantasy season makes it more likely he has all the tools required, and that he’ll do so again. (__It also shouldn’t be lost on us that rushing is a massive part of those three calculations.__)

__\*Tier Break\*__

__2\. Real-life results__ — including expected points added per dropback (EPA/DB), pressure-to-sack ratio (P2S), adjusted net yards per attempt (ANY/A), Passer Rating, and a lot of the statistical measures you might see people use to quantify real-life QB play. These are all different ways of measuring how effective a QB (within his offensive context, of course) is at sustaining drives and scoring points on an NFL field. Fantasy football and real-life value often don’t line up one-to-one, but it is an important factor; you want the offense to sustain drives and for your QB to avoid getting benched.

__\*Tier Break\*__

3\. __Everything else__ — including passing volume and production, as well as “tendency” or “style” stats like checkdown rate, catchable throw rate, or aDOT (which may have more pronounced effects on the pass-catchers’ fantasy output than on that of the QB himself).

The real-life results bucket discussed above does capture passing ability to a decent extent, so passing-only stats like total pass attempts are generally less useful for predicting fantasy output, as they’re prone to changes in environment (like a QB with a bad defense being forced to throw at higher volumes). __Additionally — unlike at every other position — passing efficiency is generally more predictive than passing volume.__ Passer rating beats out total pass attempts!

That’s enough background. Let’s get into the players!

QBs To Draft Based On The Most Predictive Fantasy Stats
-------------------------------------------------------

#### __Kyler Murray__, Minnesota Vikings

Perhaps more so than for any other QB, this analysis has left me high on Kyler Murray.

Based on Murray’s past production, I shouldn’t have needed much convincing. Since he entered the league in 2019, only three QBs average more FPG than Murray’s 19.4: Josh Allen (22.6), Lamar Jackson (22.0), and Patrick Mahomes (21.0). He’s above Jalen Hurts (19.0) and tied with Joe Burrow (19.4) and Dak Prescott (19.4). Each of these QBs goes at least 1.5 rounds earlier than Murray on *Underdog*.

More recently, seemingly every offseason since Murray tore his ACL in late 2022, I’ve scoured interviews for any sign that \*this\* would be the year Murray returns to running the football more often. I was [dubious](https://www.fantasypoints.com/nfl/articles/2025/statistically-significant-scrambles-and-qb-runs) last offseason, but in the five-game sample we got, __Murray’s 5.8 rush attempts/game (6th-most) and 34.6 rushing YPG (3rd-most) were both the most he’s posted since 2022__. Additionally, he ranked 3rd in scramble YPG (28.4). And this was all after Murray himself said he [wanted to run more](https://www.youtube.com/live/mxcLdwciVgs?si=N1r_0_u5no8_pUZl&t=5002)!

So we’ve got a scrambling profile competitive with any other QB in the league, and Murray averages 18.2 FPG (~QB13) over the past three seasons. Those are strong baselines (relative to a QB17 ADP) for rushing and fantasy production, our two most important statistical buckets.

The “real-life results” bucket is where I know Murray gives many of us pause. But understand that Kevin O’Connell has gotten exemplary play out of every veteran QB he’s ever gotten his hands on. Nick Mullens, Joshua Dobbs, and Carson Wentz have averaged 18.1 FPG across 12 full games. Do you think Murray is better than those players? I do!

 Passer Rating from Kevin O'Connell's QBs since 2021 Sam Darnold - 102.5 Kirk Cousins - 96.2 Nick Mullens - 91.8 Carson Wentz - 85.8 Joshua Dobbs - 76.4 (played his first game five days after being traded mid-season) J.J. McCarthy - 72.6 Max Brosmer - 53.0 @FantasyPtsData — Ryan Heath (@RyanJ_Heath) May 15, 2026 

To compare with the O’Connell-driven QB passer ratings above, Murray averages a 91.6 rating since his ACL tear, and has [never posted a lower rating than](https://x.com/RyanJ_Heath/status/2055358911390117952?s=20) Wentz’s in any of his last five seasons. By EPA/DB, Murray has finished 18th and 15th over the past two years; Vikings QBs ranked 29th (-0.16) in 2025 (thanks to McCarthy and Brosmer), but 13th (0.06) in every other season under O’Connell. Murray is just a completely different class of player than the Vikings’ rookies were in 2025, and base competence has always been more than enough for O’Connell.

There’s also real upside for Murray to take a step forward in his production through the air. The Vikings have ranked top-5 in red zone pass rate across all four of O’Connell’s seasons, and Murray has actually been *more* efficient playing under center (below), where O’Connell will likely shift many of his dropbacks.

 Since 2021, Kyler Murray's Cardinals rank 4th-highest in shotgun rate (71.8%) The Vikings ranked bottom-3 every year from 2021-24. Even in 2025 with Wentz/McCarthy, they ranked 8th-lowest (48.2%). However, Murray has been more efficient from under center! Via @FantasyPtsData pic.twitter.com/ORSd1C1NiM — Ryan Heath (@RyanJ_Heath) June 2, 2026 

Throw in the fact that [six of the top-nine](https://x.com/RyanJ_Heath/status/2015834333660250120?s=20) late-round QB seasons by FPG over ADP-based expectation have come from the “McShanahan” coaching tree to which O’Connell belongs, and Murray checks essentially every box. He’ll be my go-to free QB at the end of drafts this year.

#### __Bo Nix__, Denver Broncos

Starting with what matters (rushing), the most natural point of comparison for Nix is Jaxson Dart. Dart has an earlier ADP across all platforms, largely due to the perception that he offers greater rushing upside.

But I think the difference between the pair is generally overstated. Even if we only look at Dart’s starts, he averaged 7.0 rush attempts per game (~QB3) and 26.1 scramble YPG (~QB7); Nix averaged 5.3 rush attempts/game (~QB8) and 20.3 scramble YPG (~QB11), including the postseason.

The main difference has been goal-line usage — Dart received 30% (4th-most) of the Giants’ rush attempts inside the five-yard line last year, to Nix’s 5% (23rd) — but that particular type of usage is less predictive of future scoring, and can vary with circumstance. Case in point: Nix’s inside-the-five rush share doubled without J.K. Dobbins last year, __while Justin Fields’ career-lows in inside-the-five share (7.1%) and rushing TDs (2) came in 2021 under Matt Nagy, Dart’s new playcaller. Fields would go on to see 35.6____% of his team’s goal-line carries over the next four seasons without Nagy.__ In fact, neither Fields nor Mitchell Trubisky [ever exceeded](https://x.com/ChrisWechtFF/status/2018712419955093600?s=20) 3 rushing TDs across four seasons under Nagy.

If we grant that the rushing competition between Dart and Nix is unclear or even leans slightly toward Dart, Nix looks better in most other predictive metrics. From a real-life perspective, he ranked 13th in EPA/DB (0.11) and displayed elite sack avoidance, recording the lowest pressure-to-sack ratio of any QB in 2025 (8.9%). Among all QBs over the past five seasons, Nix boasts the best career pressure-to-sack ratio, topping a list containing three future first-ballot Hall of Famers!

 Best pressure-to-sack ratios since 2021 [min. 500 DBs] 1. BO NIX - 11.3% 2. Jordan Love - 12.3% 3. Josh Allen - 12.5% 4. Patrick Mahomes - 12.7% 5. Tom Brady - 14.3% 6. Brock Purdy - 14.8% ... 56. Deshaun Watson - 25.5% 57. Ryan Tannehill - 25.7% 58/last. Will Levis - 28.7% pic.twitter.com/wed32uS1Ol — Ryan Heath (@RyanJ_Heath) June 2, 2026 

Among the past five rookie QB classes, only Drake Maye, Jayden Daniels, and Brock Purdy (in a Shanahan offense that [prints EPA](https://x.com/RyanJ_Heath/status/2061899760412262416?s=20)) have averaged more EPA/DB than Nix through an initial two career seasons.

 Best EPA/DB through two seasons [since the 2021 rookie class, min. 400 dropbacks] 1. Brock Purdy - 0.28 2. Drake Maye - 0.19 3. Jayden Daniels - 0.13 4. Bo Nix - 0.09 5. Michael Penix - 0.06 6. C.J. Stroud - 0.05 7. Jaxson Dart - 0.05 (*Year 1-only) 8. Caleb Williams - 0.03 — Ryan Heath (@RyanJ_Heath) June 2, 2026 

Would it be that surprising for Nix — who averages 19.1 FPG across 36 career games, 9th-most since he entered the NFL — to take a step forward into the elite fantasy tier as Maye and Daniels have done, especially with the addition of Jaylen Waddle in Year 3?

I know the median “film bro” opinion is that Bo Nix kind of sucks. Hell, that’s mostly how I feel when I watch him. But considering that most of the stats that actually matter for fantasy football disagree, and that Sean Payton QBs have been fantasy gold for years, it’s pretty clear to me Nix would smash if he gets at all better in his third season.

 Sean Payton QBs [2018-2024] Taysom Hill: 20.5 fantasy points per start Washed Drew Brees (age: 39-41): 19.8 Bo Nix (rookie with trash receivers): 18.3 Russell Wilson: 18.0 Trevor Siemian: 18.0 Jameis Winston: 17.2 Teddy Bridgewater: 17.1 For perspective, Nix currently ranks as… — Scott Barrett (@ScottBarrettDFB) November 18, 2024 

#### __Justin Herbert__, Los Angeles Chargers

Justin Herbert is an [athletic clone of Josh Allen](https://x.com/ScottBarrettDFB/status/1951018279159419386?s=20), who ran the ball much more than you remember last year. Herbert ranked 6th among QBs in rushing YPG (31.1, ahead of Jalen Hurts and Lamar Jackson), 1st in scramble yards (439, ahead of Drake Maye), and tied for 5th in total rush attempts (83, ahead of Caleb Williams). He’s being drafted at least a round later on *Underdog* than all three of the QBs I just mentioned.

Of course, it’s exciting that Herbert gets to play under new OC Mike McDaniel in 2026, who engineered a season in which Tua Tagovailoa led the NFL in passing yards (4,624) and ranked 2nd in ANY/A (7.48), while the offense posted the 3rd-most in yards per play (6.4) of any team over the past five years.

But the more impactful change might be that Herbert gets LT Joe Alt back healthy this year. Herbert has already showcased top-shelf efficiency and fantasy production with Alt on the field:

 Justin Herbert ... In 4 games with Joe Alt for over 50% snaps: * 67.7% comp rate * 8.2 YPA * 272 yards per game * 6.8% TD rate * 1.5% INT rate * 8.3% sack rate In other 12 games: * 66.0% comp rate * 7.0 YPA * 220 yards per game * 4.5% TD rate * 2.9% INT rate * 10.0% sack rate — Jared Smola (@SmolaDS) January 29, 2026 

Herbert’s 6.8% TD rate within the four-game split with Alt that Jared Smola highlights above would have ranked 4th-best last year (behind only Matthew Stafford, Brock Purdy, and Lamar Jackson. __His 22.4 FPG in that sample would have trailed only Josh Allen, and his 0.44 EPA/DB would have easily led every QB over any of the past five seasons!__ One could seriously argue he’d have won MVP had Alt stayed healthy.

And best of all, Herbert’s rushing production doesn’t seem to have been an artifact of him simply running for his life without Alt. His scramble rate increased from 8.2% to 10.1% with Alt playing in the above sample, while his overall rushing YPG also slightly increased to 32.8. The offense just worked so much better that all aspects of Herbert’s game were more productive.

Herbert may well be the earliest QB I’ll actually consider clicking come managed redraft season, as I’d put his upside up against any QB going ahead of him besides Josh Allen.

#### __Malik Willis__, Miami Dolphins

If this were 2019-2021 (in my mind, the golden era of arguing about NFL analytics online), you’d have heard a lot more about Malik Willis’s EPA this offseason.

On 117 dropbacks over the past two seasons, Willis easily leads the NFL in EPA/DB (0.47), nearly double that of 2nd-place Josh Allen (0.24). Since 2021, the best single season by EPA/DB is Lamar Jackson’s 2024 (0.35), coming in at 25% less efficient than Willis.

It’s obviously tempting to dismiss that as a small sample, but maybe that’s selling Willis short. Elite small-sample EPA spotted rookie Brock Purdy and Panthers Sam Darnold years before they were broadly considered to be good QBs!

 Best seasons by EPA/dropback in "small sample" years since 2021 [Between 100-200 dropbacks] 1. Malik Willis with the Packers in 2024-25: 0.47 2. Brock Purdy as a rookie in 2022: 0.20 3. Sam Darnold with the Panthers in 2022: 0.17 A pretty unreal track record at the top tbh — Ryan Heath (@RyanJ_Heath) June 3, 2026 

Even sweeter for fantasy football, the EPA/dropback stat I’m referencing doesn’t include designed runs — only what happens on dropbacks (e.g., pass attempts, scrambles, and sacks). And a majority of Willis’s rushing fantasy production (53%) came on designed runs!

Naturally, Willis leads all QBs in fantasy points per dropback (0.72) and fantasy points per opportunity (0.75) over the same two-year sample. He averaged 23.6 fantasy points per start across three contests with the Packers, a mark that would have tied with Josh Allen for the most FPG of any QB last year. He also averaged 7.0 rush attempts and 58.0 rushing YPG over that sample — marks that would have ranked 3rd-best and best last year.

So on the sample we have, Willis checks the boxes of per-game production, rushing, and per-dropback efficiency with flying colors. There’s definitely a world in which he scores as a top-12 fantasy QB that you can get off the waiver wire in your home league this year.

But also, Willis really tests the limits of any statistical analysis. Sure, passing volume doesn’t correlate well with fantasy production in the aggregate, but will that hold at this new extreme, where we find Willis with just a career-high 21 pass attempts in a game?

 Pass attempts by Malik Willis in all his career starts 10 16 23 14 19 21 3 total passing TDs, one game over 70 receiving yards for a pass-catcher (the GOAT Christian Watson) https://t.co/EdBbaWvCBG — Ryan Heath (@RyanJ_Heath) May 15, 2026 

Willis also sports a bottom-10 pressure-to-sack ratio among 62 qualifying QBs over the past two seasons (23.9%), with Geno Smith and Deshaun Watson the only starting QBs to fare worse than him. Though the Dolphins bolstered their offensive line with 12th overall pick Kadyn Proctor, it’s pretty easy to imagine drive-ending sacks killing this offense every time they hit 3rd-and-7 if Willis doesn’t improve his sack avoidance. With De’Von Achane the only relevant pass-catcher on the team and the offense [ranking bottom-3](https://x.com/ConnorAllenNFL/status/2056797975402217775?s=20) in Vegas implied points per game, this could be one of the least-productive passing offenses of the modern NFL era.

All told, Kyler Murray’s larger sample of past success and vastly superior offensive environment will likely make him my free late-round QB of choice for 1QB redraft leagues, rather than Willis. The ~two-round premium on Murray over Willis in best ball ADP also makes perfect sense to me. But even if there’s a 65% chance the Dolphins totally crash and burn, selecting Willis is sort of like getting to select Anthony Richardson back in 2024 (with [similarly gaudy small-sample rushing efficiency metrics](https://www.fantasypoints.com/nfl/articles/2024/statistically-significant-fantasy-points-per-dropback#/)) if he were a late-round pick instead of the consensus QB6. The risk clearly doesn’t matter for Willis at cost (~QB21) when put in that light.

#### __Jayden Daniels__, Washington Commanders

I’m largely just going to focus on Daniels’ rushing numbers, as they’re both the most important consideration and hold the most intrigue for me. Despite an injury-plagued year, he led all QBs in rush attempts per game (8.3) and rushing YPG (39.7) in 2025 while ranking 4th-best in rushing XFP/G (4.3).

There’s a perception and fear that Daniels may not run the ball as much in 2025 after missing 10 games to injury. Worse, Kliff Kingsbury and his fast-paced offense were run out of town by HC Dan Quinn, who reportedly [wanted the offense to play more slowly to help the defense](https://www.espn.com/nfl/story/_/id/47528237/sources-kingsbury-whitt-commanders-coordinators). With new OC David Blough set to play [less from the shotgun and more from under center](https://x.com/UnderdogNFL/status/2021290400674349136?s=20), will that all translate to less play volume and less scrambling for Daniels?

I don’t really believe so! While Kingsbury was outlierishly fast-paced in Arizona (averaging 64.2 plays per game, which would have led all playcallers in 2025), that wasn’t nearly as true of his offenses in Washington. There, he sat at just 58.9 plays per game over the past two seasons, which would have ranked almost perfectly league-average. Especially compared to Daniels’ starts in 2025 (57.0 plays per game, ~26th), the play volume doesn’t have much room to fall.

__Moreover, Daniels has actually posted a__ *__higher__* __scramble rate on dropbacks from under center and the pistol (21.3% on 94 career dropbacks) than from the shotgun (12.0% on 749 dropbacks).__ The same pattern holds for all QBs league-wide (5.3% scramble rate from shotgun, 5.7% scramble rate from under center) and for certain other mobile QBs like Kyler Murray (5.9% from shotgun, 11.5% from under center) or Drake Maye (10.0% from shotgun, 13.0% from under center) over the past two seasons. There’s no reason I can see to believe the change in offensive style might reduce Daniels’ rushing volume; in fact, it could well increase it!

Even without getting into the weeds on the offense, Daniels fell from 44.0 rushing YPG pre-hamstring injury in 2025 to just 33.5 in the two games after he returned. That feels destined to come back up with Daniels’ lower body healthy again, and I have no major concerns about his long-term viability from a real-life perspective; over the past two seasons, Daniels ranks 12th-best by CPOE (+3.7%), 11th-best by EPA/DB (0.13), and 13th-best by passer rating (96.7) among 43 qualifying QBs.

Most actionably, the injuries and offensive uncertainty have created a buy window on Daniels in dynasty superflex formats, in which I’d love to acquire him for anything short of ~three 1sts while that’s still possible.

##### __{{Saquon Barkley|RB|PHI}}__ (Phi) over 1000.5 rushing yards (-130, theSCORE Bet)

+ __Why I like the over__: Barkley came crashing back to earth last season after becoming just the ninth player to run for more than 2000+ yards, even while sitting out the season finale with a division title wrapped up. He still reached 280 carries and 1140 yards despite Philly’s offense cratering in EPA/play (.07 Risk 1.15 units to win 1 unit. [Placed June 8](https://www.fantasypoints.com/nfl/articles/2026/brolleys-best-bets-nfl-futures#/).

Montgomery requested a trade after his opportunities dipped once __Dan Campbell__ took over playcalling in Week 10. Detroit granted his wish by sending him to Houston for __Juice Scruggs__, a 2026 fourth-round pick, and a 2027 seventh-round pick, and the Texans immediately locked him into a two-year deal that included $10 million guaranteed. Houston has big plans for its new lead back after __Joe Mixon__’s season-long absence forced __Woody Marks__ into a role he wasn’t ready to handle.

Monty has cleared 716+ rushing yards in each of his first seven seasons, including the last two years in Detroit as the #2 option behind __Jahmyr Gibbs__. He logged just a 39% carry share in 31 games in 2024-25, but his workload will significantly climb as Houston’s new lead runner. Monty is Houston’s latest hired hand at the position, following in __Joe Mixon__’s path from the 2024 season. Mixon, at 28 years old, turned in 245/1016/11 rushing on a 66.9% carry share in his only season with the Texans.

Montgomery averaged 4.2 YPC or better in each of his three seasons for the Lions, including a strong 4.53 YPC last season when he ranked 12th in YACO/ATT (2.45). Houston’s offensive line needed a significant upgrade after ranking 30th in adjusted YBC/ATT (1.45) and 30th in success rate (45.1%) last season. The Texans beefed up their offensive line by selecting __Keylan Rutledge__ at No. 26, which came after they acquired __Braden Smith__ and __Wyatt Teller__ earlier this offseason. Monty has also been fairly durable, never missing more than four games in any season.

full_text:
The NFL is in “Phase Three” of the offseason, the final stage before contact practices begin with training camp in late July. We’ve seen a steady stream of news since OTAs (organized team activities) started in mid-May, and it always gets a little more interesting in June when veteran players are required to report for one mandatory minicamp unless they have an excused absence.

I went team by team to round up the most important fantasy headlines coming out of all 32 workouts. I’ll update this article through June 18, the final day of team activities in Phase Three. Check back often for regular updates!

\>Each news item will have a date at the end of it for when it was updated or added to the article…ADP data used in this article is based on the last month of drafts with our partners over at [Underdog Fantasy](https://www.fantasypoints.com/underdog#/)…Subscribe to our [Fantasy Bundle Package](https://www.fantasypoints.com/plans#/) to take your NFL research to the next level!

{{CTA|Underdog|omit=\[none\]}}

June 9
------

##### __Jacksonville Jaguars__

+   __Chris Rodriguez__ has been absent from OTAs for what was previously an [undisclosed injury](https://www.si.com/nfl/jaguars/onsi/jacksonville-winners-losers-2nd-week-otas-antonio-johnson), with __Liam Coen__ saying, “The injury report will come out at some point.” It wasn’t the best sign that Coen is avoiding giving any details on the injury. At this time of the year, most coaches will tell reporters if it’s a minor issue, so it’s a sign it could be a more significant injury. We found out that he needed [surgery on his left foot](https://www.jacksonville.com/story/sports/nfl/jaguars/2026/06/08/jacksonville-jaguars-chris-rodriguez-nfl/90465270007/?gnt-cfr=1&gca-cat=p&gca-uir=false&gca-epti=z111701p001750c001750e000200v111701&gca-ft=50&gca-ds=sophi), but he’s expected to be ready for training camp. Rodriguez has some familiarity with a Coen offense from their time together in Kentucky, but his time away from the field is giving __Bhaysul Tuten__ an even longer runway to grab the lead role in what is shaping up to be a committee backfield, with __LeQuint Allen__ involved as a pass pro specialist. Rodriguez has been a shaky pick at his soon-to-be falling ADP (118, RB37), while Tuten may get a little too expensive if his ADP (60, RB25) rises to the early fifth round. *(Updated June 9)*

##### __New York Giants__

+   __Cam Skattebo__ took part in individual drills at mandatory minicamp, which is a good sign as he pushes to be ready for training camp and to avoid the PUP list. He’s a little over seven months removed from his right ankle dislocation, fibula fracture, and deltoid ligament rupture from late October. Skattebo and __Quinshon Judkins__ are both returning from fractured fibulas, with Judkins progressing to team drills at Browns OTAs in early June. Ryan Heath [laid out](https://x.com/RyanJ_Heath/status/2056752913913991666) how players returning from similar injuries have been fantasy potholes in the recent past. Skattebo remains atop New York’s depth chart ahead of __Tyrone Tracy__ after the Giants passed on adding to the backfield. He has a chance to replicate his success from his rookie season when he ranked as the RB9 with 16.1 FP, but he’ll need to prove he’s healthy enough to warrant another large workload in training camp and early in the season. *(Added June 9)*

##### __Los Angeles Rams__

+   Starting left tackle __Alaric Jackson__ was arrested on June 8 on a felony domestic violence charge. NBC4 in Los Angeles [reported](https://www.nbclosangeles.com/news/local/lapd-la-ram-alaric-jackson-arrested-for-domestic-battery/3901536/) that Jackson thought he was being recorded and allegedly tried to take the phone from the woman, and investigators said the victim had scratch marks on her arms. It isn’t the first time Jackson has had issues with phone recordings. He previously served a two-game suspension at the start of the 2024 season for violating the NFL’s Personal Conduct Policy, but the nature of the violation was not clear at the time. He was later named in a civil lawsuit in November 2025 for allegedly recording a woman during sex without her consent and refusing to delete the video despite her requests in May of 2024. Jackson could be looking at more than a six-game suspension if the NFL disciplines him for the latest incident, since it is his second offense of the Personal Conduct Policy. The Rams would have a massive hole at left tackle in front of a 38-year-old quarterback with a creaky back if Jackson faces a suspension, but there’s a chance the process drags through this season. *(Added June 9)*

June 8
------

##### __Indianapolis Colts__

+   __Tyler Warren__ has been checking out his A.S.S. this offseason after finishing as one of the worst separators at the position. He ranked 37th out of 40 TEs in our Average Separation Score metric (-.025). Warren wants to be more explosive in his second season, specifically when he’s changing directions. Warren [told ESPN](https://www.espn.com/nfl/story/_/id/48968602/colts-tyler-warren-seeks-more-explosiveness-second-season), “A big thing \[is\] the explosion out of my breaks. Getting in the break is one thing, but being able to accelerate out of it and still you create the space, but being able to hold that space if you are running across the field…I think it’s big.” He showed plenty of explosiveness when he had the ball in his hands, ranking fourth in YAC/REC (6.50) and second in YAC (494) behind only __Trey McBride__. He finished as the TE11 with 11.1 FPG as a rookie, but he reached double-digit FP just once in his final seven games, which corresponded with __Daniel Jones__ rupturing his Achilles. Warren will take on a bigger role in the passing game with __Michael Pittman__ leaving behind a team-high 21.1% target share, and he’ll need Jones to be close to full health to pay off his ADP (66, TE4). *(Added June 8)*

##### __Kansas City Chiefs__

+   We got a brief taste of __Kenneth Walker__ after __Zach Charbonnet__ tore his ACL in the Divisional Round, and fantasy owners wanted more of it in the future. He could get the role in Kansas City after the Chiefs handed him $28.7 million guaranteed in free agency, but OC __Eric Bieniemy__ [wants Walker to improve](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=013-ov6fnOk) in all areas of the passing game. Bieneiemy said, “I want Kenneth to work at is just understanding that we just have to become a better player when the ball is not in our hand. I know exactly what he’s going to do and what he’s capable of when the ball is in his hands. So, now when the ball is not in his hands, what value is he going to add? We have to do a great job protecting the quarterback, and then we got to do a great job of being a route runner on the perimeter.” Walker ceded work to Charbonnet in the passing game last season, finishing behind him in route share (32.2%<34.7%) and snap share (46.1%<48.9%). Walker exploded in three playoff games when he stepped into a bell-cow role, posting 65/313/4 rushing and 9/104 receiving for 24.9 FPG. His postseason performance was better than __Christian McCaffrey__’s RB1 performance of 24.5 FPG in the regular season. Walker has legit top-five upside at the position if he can grab a pass-down role, but the Chiefs have three passing back options after signing __Emari Demercado__ and drafting __Emmett Johnson__ to go along with __Brashard Smith__ — Demercado has consistently worked as the [#2 RB](https://atozsports.com/nfl/kansas-city-chiefs-news/chiefs-players-trending-right-direction-otas-mandatory-minicamp/) during OTAs. It’s a storyline to follow in training camp and early in the season. *(Added June 8)*

##### __Carolina Panthers__

+   *The Charlotte Observer*’s Mike Kaye [believes](https://www.charlotteobserver.com/sports/nfl/carolina-panthers/article315949969.html) __Chuba Hubbard__ will take “the lion’s share of touches” early in the season, but he could cede more work to __Jonathon Brooks__ as the season moves along if he proves capable of handling it. Kaye also wrote that the team will test Brooks in training camp to test him and get him up to speed after a lengthy layoff. Brooks has appeared in just three games since November 2023 because of a pair of torn ACLs in the same knee. Hubbard finished as the RB13 in 2024 with 16.3 FPG, but is coming off a down season and lost work to __Rico Dowdle__ because of a calf injury. Among RBs with 100+ carries in a season, Hubbard is the only RB who failed to break a single 15-yard run in a full season during the Fantasy Points Data era (2021-25). The Panthers showed some faith in Brooks and __Trevor Etienne__ by allowing Dowdle to walk while not bringing in any significant competition for the #2 RB spot. Hubbard is the better pick (71, RB26) than Brooks if you pass on drafting your RB2 through your first 5-6 picks, while Brooks is a reach at his surging ADP (110, RB36). *(Added June 8)*

##### __Houston Texans__

+   Texans reporter Aaron Wilson [wrote](https://www.click2houston.com/sports/2026/06/07/texans-have-big-plans-for-receiver-jayden-higgins-playing-faster-playing-stronger-going-to-have-a-great-year/) that __Jayden Higgins__ is showing signs of a potential breakout in his second season. He noted that he’s been a standout at the position, lining up in multiple spots, showing improved chemistry with __C.J. Stroud__, and looking stronger and more explosive. HC __DeMeco Ryans__ said, “You see a physical difference. You see a stronger, more chiseled-out receiver. We step on the field, he’s playing faster. He’s playing stronger. He’s making all of the tough catches. He’s playing extremely fast. He’s taken advantage of his offseason, and he’s really improved in a ton of areas. The first area for him is how can we play fast consistently and he’s doing that right now. He’s going to have a great year.” Higgins posted a respectable 1.54 YPRR and .20 TPRR as a second-round pick last season, but he finished behind __Xavier Hutchinson__ and __Christian Kirk__ with a 52.8% route share. He ran just 21.4% of his routes from the slot last season, and lining up in more spots could help him run more routes. He needs to separate from Hutchinson, __Jaylin Noel__, and __Tank Dell__ to have any chance of becoming a fantasy-relevant WR, and his upside will be capped by target-hog __Nico Collins__. *(Added June 8)*

##### __Arizona Cardinals__

+   __Jacoby Brissett__ wasn’t present for the start of Arizona’s voluntary OTAs but is present at mandatory minicamp. He’s seeking a pay raise on his $4.88 million contract, with just $1.5 million guaranteed for the 2026 season. He’s still being paid like a backup despite the organization [informing him](https://www.espn.com/mlb/story/_/id/48810874/without-jacoby-brissett-mike-lafleur-cardinals-open-otas) that he would open the season as the starter. ESPN’s Josh Weinfuss reported that the two sides remained “significantly” apart as of May 22. Arizona handed __Gardner Minshew__ $5.14 million in guaranteed money in free agency before selecting __Carson Beck__ at No. 65, so Brissett is unlikely to get a hefty raise before the season. Brissett is missing out on reps in a new offense, but __Mike LaFleur__ said he wasn’t concerned about the 10-year veteran falling behind. He ranked as the QB7 (19.9 FPG) from Week 6 through the end of the season, but he won’t drop back 45.8 times per game as he did last season. Brissett isn’t the easiest click in best ball drafts, even at this suppressed ADP (190, QB30). The Cards are likely to be out of postseason contention, and they’ll want to take a look at Beck during the best ball money-making weeks. Brissett is much more intriguing in 2-QB/Superflex redraft leagues if you want to punt your second-QB spot until the middle rounds of the draft and use Brissett until he eventually is benched later in the season. *(Updated June 8)*

##### __New England Patriots__

+   __Kayshon Boutte__ worked out [away from the team](https://www.espn.com/nfl/story/_/id/48780703/new-england-patriots-notebook-longest-tenured-employee-nancy-meier-retire) facility during New England’s voluntary offseason program, but he said he’ll report to mandatory minicamp. Boutte is on a rookie contract as a 2023 sixth-round pick, so he’s likely looking to avoid being fined more than anything by reporting. Boutte isn’t going to have much of a role after the Patriots acquired __A.J. Brown__ and __Romeo Doubs__, and New England would love to move Boutte for a late-round pick after sending a fifth-round pick to Philadelphia. Boutte doesn’t have any fantasy value right now, but he could become a deep league option if he’s traded to a WR-needy team later this summer. *(Added June 8)*

June 5
------

##### __Houston Texans__

+   __Tank Dell__ participated in non-contact team drills during OTAs after primarily working off to the side in May. He suffered a catastrophic knee injury in late December of his sophomore season and hasn’t seen NFL action since then. Dell could be one of the best feel-good stories of the season if he’s able to regain most of his previous form and make Houston’s roster out of training camp. He’s still off the fantasy radar until his explosiveness and his playing time opportunities return. *(Added June 5)*

##### __Seattle Seahawks__

+   __A.J. Barner__ [revealed](https://x.com/BradyHenderson/status/2062670865154838902) that he underwent two surgeries after Seattle’s Super Bowl run for a pair of undisclosed injuries. He’s yet to miss a game in his two-year career, but he played through multiple ailments and finished on the injury report in Week 10 with a calf issue. He said he’s feeling better but will be ready to go for training camp. Barner’s situation is one to monitor in case he falls behind in his recovery, which would open up more opportunities for __Elijah Arroyo__. *(Added June 5)*

June 4
------

##### __Chicago Bears__

+   __Rome Odunze__ missed the final five games of the regular season for a stress fracture last season, and he’s still dealing with complications from the break this offseason. He [told the media](https://apnews.com/article/chicago-bears-rome-odunze-edece1a9ebd209066f9925d58c493981), “It’s not from a standpoint that I’m like always in pain, but the way my foot broke, there’s calluses in there that creates a different type of foot structure with those bones — different things that kind of shifts things around. So my new normal was kind of what I am going into. And I don’t think that’s anything that’s going to prohibit me or keep me from making plays.” The Bears weren’t too concerned about his injury situation when they moved on from __DJ Moore__ and __Olamide Zaccheaus__ this offseason without adding much to their receiving corps outside of __Kalif Raymond__. I’m not avoiding Odunze at his ADP (55, WR28) for his candor with the Bears media, but it’s a situation to at least be aware of if it flares up later in training camp or during the season. It does make me much more willing to select __Luther Burden__ (42, WR21) and __Colston Loveland__ (46, TE3) at their aggressive ADPs just in case Odunze isn’t quite right in his third season. *(Added June 4)*

##### __Green Bay Packers__

+   __Micah Parsons__ [confirmed](https://www.espn.com/nfl/story/_/id/48958480/packers-micah-parsons-return-least-mid-october) he won’t be ready for the start of the season, which means he’s likely to open the season on the PUP list, which will cost him at least four games. Parsons said, “The goal isn't for me to go out there and re-hurt myself trying to force myself to get back the first few games. The goal has always been \[to be available for the\] playoffs, and I think we're all on the same page.” Parsons injured his left knee in mid-December and needed surgery on his ACL and meniscus. He revealed the Packers have a nine-month rule for players coming back from ACL injuries, especially when there are other repairs associated with it. Green Bay’s defense will be a little weaker early in the season, which could force __Jordan Love__ and the offense to play in some higher-scoring games while Parsons catches up to speed. *(Added June 4)*

+   The Packers and __Christian Watson__ agreed to terms on a four-year, $110.5 million contract extension, which includes a $31 million signing bonus. He’s coming off career-highs in receptions per game (3.5), receiving YPG (61.1), and FPG (13.2, WR17) after missing the first seven games of the season for an ACL injury in the 2024 season finale. The Packers are putting their trust in Watson with a contract extension and by thinning out their WR corps, letting __Romeo Doubs__ walk to New England and trading __Dontayvion Wicks__ to Philadelphia. Green Bay ranked in the bottom 10 of pass rate over expectation in each of the last two seasons, but it may be forced to be more pass-heavy because of __Josh Jacobs__’s legal situation and __Micah Parsons__’ recovery. Watson has top-12 upside if he can stay healthy, and he’s one of the best picks on the board at his generous ADP (60, WR30). *(Added June 4)*

##### __Detroit Lions/Atlanta Falcons__

+   __Dan Campbell__ articulated what we’ve all known since the Lions traded __David Montgomery__ to the Texans this offseason, calling __Jahmyr Gibbs__ the team’s bell-cow back, which was the role he started to take on once Campbell took over playcalling in Week 10 last season. Gibbs and __Bijan Robinson__ are not only jockeying to be the first pick in fantasy drafts this summer, but they’re also battling to be the highest-paid player at the running back position. Gibbs and Robinson are both eligible for contract extensions heading into their fourth seasons, and ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler [reported](https://x.com/ESPNNFL/status/2060461475534094576?s=20) in late May that Gibbs is seeking $20 million per year or more. __Saquon Barkley__ is the only running back north of $20 million per year with an AAV of $20.6 million. Whoever signs later between Gibbs and Bijan is likely to become the highest-paid player at the position. *(Updated June 4)*

##### __Indianapolis Colts__

+   __Alec Pierce__ is still on the mend from offseason ankle surgery, but he isn’t participating in OTAs or mandatory minicamp. __Shane Steichen__ [said](https://coltswire.usatoday.com/story/sports/nfl/colts/2026/06/02/shane-steichen-provides-injury-update-colts-alec-pierce-during-otas/90368106007/) Pierce is doing well in his rehab and is on track to be ready for training camp. The Colts clearly weren’t too concerned about his injury since they handed him a four-year, $114 million contract, which included $84 million guaranteed. Pierce ranked first in aDOT (19.4), YPR (21.34), and YPT (11.94) and fourth in air yards share (43%) among 76 WRs who saw 50+ targets last season. He did it while running the second-highest rate of routes out wide (89%) behind __George Pickens__. Pierce became the team’s #1 receiver this past season, and Indy traded __Michael Pittman__ to the Steelers to create cap space to keep him around. Pierce remains a volatile weekly fantasy option because of the boom-or-bust nature of his targets, but he’s a potential league-winning WR3 (75, WR36) if he continues his ascent from the last two years and if he sees more targets with Pittman out of the picture. *(Added June 4)*

##### __San Francisco 49ers__

+   __George Kittle__ [believes](https://www.espn.com/nfl/story/_/id/48960408/niners-kittle-achilles-targets-week-1-says-track) he’s on track to be ready for the season opener in Australia despite tearing his right Achilles in mid-January and having it surgically repaired 19 weeks ago. He’s yet to be cleared for football activities, but he resumed 100% body weight jogging a few weeks ago and was seen doing single-leg hops on the side during OTAs. ESPN’s Nick Wagoner points out that a complicating factor could be San Francisco’s travel plans for the season opener Down Under. The 49ers are set to leave on Sept. 2 before they play the Rams on Sept. 11, and the long flight could also be a concern if it affects his recovery. I still believe that the 49ers won’t rush the 33-year-old TE onto the field in September despite his seemingly quick recovery. He’s a tough click for me despite his significantly reduced ADP (119, TE9) from last summer. *(Added June 4)*

##### __Pittsburgh Steelers__

+   The Steelers signed __Darnell Washington__ to a four-year, $42 million extension, which includes $21 million in guaranteed money. Washington is generously listed at 264 pounds at 6’7”, and he’s been used as a third offensive tackle in Pittsburgh’s offense. He’s coming off career-highs in receptions (31), receiving yards (364), and snap share (57%) in his third season. He’ll continue to be a thorn in the side of the much more fantasy-friendly __Pat Freiermuth__, who is a late-round dart throw (188, TE27). It’s also a slight knock to __Germie Bernard__ (178, WR70) since __Mike McCarthy__ is likely to use more 2-TE sets than he previously did in Dallas — they finished second in 11 personnel snaps (749) in his final season with the Cowboys. *(Added June 4)*

##### __San Francisco 49ers__

+   The Santa Clara District Attorney’s Office [issued an arrest warrant](https://www.espn.com/nfl/story/_/id/48958203/warrant-issued-49ers-brandon-aiyuk-viral-speeding-video) for __Brandon Aiyuk__ on a misdemeanor charge of exhibition of speeding. He posted a [video on YouTube](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=kpsZ8IP46BU) of himself driving well over the posted 40 mph speed limit on a road that runs past Levi’s Stadium. Aiyuk is unlikely to face jail time or a suspension from the NFL, but it does make it more unlikely that the 49ers will be able to trade him before the start of the season. The 49ers continue to stick it to Aiyuk by refusing to release him at this point, and it takes a leap of faith to think he’ll be a fantasy asset in 2026 if he eventually latches onto a team. Aiyuk hasn’t played good football since 2023, and he’s a waste of a pick even at his rock-bottom ADP (177, WR69). *(Added June 4)*

June 3
------

##### __Arizona Cardinals__

+   __Mike LaFleur__ [told reporters](https://x.com/theo_mackie/status/2061916646542016616?s=20) that __Marvin Harrison__ will play the __Davante Adams__ role as the X receiver in his offense, and __Michael Wilson__ will play the __Puka Nacua__ role as the Z receiver. Additionally, __Kendrick Bourne__ will see more time in the slot as the #3 WR after running 28.3% of his routes from the slot over the last five seasons. The bad news for Arizona’s WRs is that __Jacoby Brissett__, __Gardner Minshew__, and __Carson Beck__ will be playing the __Matthew Stafford__ role. It’s a slight upgrade for Wilson since Puka ran far more of his routes from the slot than Adams (35% to 14%) last season. On the other hand, Adams saw far more end-zone targets (27 to 5) and inside-the-20 targets (32 to 17) than Puka. Harrison is looking for a breakout campaign in his third season, but he said he’s trying to get back to 100% health after two heel injuries. He [said](https://www.espn.com/nfl/story/_/id/48951972/cardinals-harrison-not-recovered-25-injuries), “I don’t think it’s going to linger into next season, for sure. The thing with your feet, you use them all the time. That makes the process take probably a little longer than maybe usually.” Harrison (68, WR33) is being overdrafted, and Wilson (92, WR43) is being underdrafted in early drafts, and they could see their ADPs pinched together more as the summer moves along. *(Added June 3)*

##### __Green Bay Packers__

+   __Josh Jacobs__ was arrested in Wisconsin on domestic abuse charges in connection with a disturbance on May 23. He was booked into Brown County Jail on five charges for the domestic violence incident, including felony strangulation and four misdemeanors. The NFL said that it is aware of the report and is in contact with the Packers, and Jacobs “vehemently” denied the allegations through his lawyers. The Brown County District Attorney’s Office released Jacobs from custody on May 27. No charges were filed at the time, but the investigation remains open, and a final charging decision will be made at a later date. Jacobs is coming off an RB10 finish (15.9 FPG) in his seventh season, and he was set up for a massive role once again entering his age-28 season, with just __Chris Brooks__, __MarShawn Lloyd__, and __Pierre Strong__ behind him on the depth chart. The investigation and legal process are likely to drag through the 2026 season unless charges are dropped or pled down. However, the NFL could place him on the commissioner’s exempt list during the investigation, especially because the charges involve domestic violence. I’m leaning toward Jacobs not facing a suspension this season in the initial stages of the investigation, but that could dramatically change in the upcoming weeks if incriminating photos or details emerge. Jacobs was back on the practice field on June 2, and __Matt LaFleur__ said it was “[business as usual](https://www.espn.com/nfl/story/_/id/48949345/josh-jacobs-packers-practice-prosecutors-mull-charges)” when asked about the veteran RB’s participation in practice while being under investigation for alleged domestic abuse. Jacobs will have to fall into the fourth round for me to consider selecting him as my #2 RB as things stand right now. Brooks is worth a late-round stab in case Jacobs’ situation gets worse, and Arizona RBs __James Conner__ or __Trey Benson__ could eventually be in play for the Packers if Jacobs is in danger of missing time. Stay tuned for this developing story. *(Updated June 3)*

##### __Cleveland Browns__

+   __Quinshon Judkins__ participated in voluntary minicamp in late April and in voluntary OTA workouts on May 20, which is five months after he suffered a dislocated ankle and a fractured fibula, which required surgery on Dec. 23. His initial recovery timeline called for 4-6 months off before returning to football activity, so it appears he’s on track to be ready for training camp. He took another step toward that goal by participating in team drills at a [June 3 OTA workout](https://x.com/ScottPetrak/status/2062216969491755051). Judkins and __Cam Skattebo__ are both returning from fractured fibulas. Ryan Heath [laid out](https://x.com/RyanJ_Heath/status/2056752913913991666) how players returning from similar injuries have been fantasy potholes in the recent past. Judkins is looking to break that trend behind a revamped offensive line in __Todd Monken__’s new offense. He should rack up plenty of carries to justify selecting him as an RB2 at his fifth-round ADP (55, RB23), but it’s tough to build a massive upside case since he could lose passing-game snaps to __Dylan Sampson__ in what is shaping up to be a spread offense. *(Updated June 3)*

##### __New England Patriots__

+   The Patriots lost blocking TE __Julian Hill__ to a season-ending injury in practice, placing him on the IR to make room for recently acquired __A.J. Brown__. Hill landed a surprising three-year, $15 million contract in free agency, which included $7.5 million guaranteed, and he was set to replace __Austin Hooper__ as the #2 TE behind __Hunter Henry__. Hill played on 55% of the snaps for the Dolphins last season, posting a 20.9% route share and a 5.4% target share in 14 games. Third-round pick __Eli Raridon__ could be pushed into a bigger role than anticipated during his rookie season. Henry could get a slight boost in his route share because of the injury after running 72.3% of the routes next to Hooper, who ran 32.1% of the routes. He also added that Concepcion has been moved around the formation and used in heavy motion in early installs as they try to “hunt favorable matchups” for their first-round WR. __Zay Flowers__ flourished under __Todd Monken__ in Baltimore, and Monken will use Concepcion like Flowers. The biggest concern for Concepcion is the quarterback play he’ll receive from __Deshaun Watson__ and __Shedeur Sanders__, but he’s worth betting on at [+3000 odds](https://www.fantasypoints.com/nfl/articles/betting/2026/nfl-rookie-of-the-year-awards#/) to win the Offensive Rookie of the Year. *(Added May 26)*

##### __Philadelphia Eagles__

+   __Jalen Hurts__ is set to have a new playcaller for the 11th straight season since he enrolled at Alabama for the 2016 season. __Sean Mannion__ is taking over for __Kevin Patullo__ for the 2026 season, and he comes from a __Sean McVay__\-__Matt LaFleur__ background. *The Athletic*’s Zach Berman wrote that Mannion’s new scheme will include more under-center plays, including play-action from under center. ##### __Free Agent__

+   Former Dolphins WR __Tyreek Hill__ may not be ready to play until the middle of the season, [per Adam Schefter](https://www.nbcsports.com/fantasy/football/player-news?p=2). The free agent WR suffered multiple ligament tears and a knee dislocation in the fourth game of last season. Hill has relied heavily on speed and quickness, and it’s fair to wonder if he’ll have the same twitchiness entering his age-32 season, if he’s able to play at all in 2026. It also doesn’t help that he brings plenty of off-the-field baggage with him to his next location. Hill may have to wait until the start of the season to land a short-term, incentive-laden contract once he’s able to prove he’s healthy and close to playing football again. *(Added May 24)*

##### __Las Vegas Raiders__

+   __Ashton Jeanty__ is being drafted like he’ll be a bell-cow back with a first-round ADP (12, RB6), but __Klint Kubiak__ notably rotated __Kenneth Walker__ and __Zach Charbonnet__ in Seattle last season. The Raiders also selected __Mike Washington__ in the fourth round, but Kubiak is ready to get plenty of mileage out of Jeanty this season. Kubiak said, “It’s important to have a quality second back, but the best player has got to play, and we’ve got to get them on the field as much as we can…Christian McCaffrey, his play-snap percentage is high. So, those great backs, they don’t want to come off the field.” Jeanty also spoke about staying on the field as much as possible after he finished fourth in snap share (77.9%), second in carry share (72.1%), and seventh in route share (52.2%) as a rookie. Jeanty’s path to a massive role is intact unless Washington forces Kubiak to get him involved with a strong training camp. Jeanty needs a better offensive environment and better blocking — he finished second to last in YBC/ATT (1.28) — to pay off his current ADP. *(Added May 22)*

##### __Los Angeles Chargers__

+   GM __Joe Hortiz__ [told Kay Adams](https://x.com/UpAndAdamsShow/status/2057491131907113435?s=20) that the team hasn’t “closed the door” on __Keenan Allen__ returning to the franchise for a 13th season. He also said, “We’re letting these young guys get a chance…Our guys that we have here, we’re letting them grow and develop.” The next month of practices will decide whether the Chargers go into training camp with __Ladd McConkey__, __Quentin Johnston__, __Tre’ Harris__, __KeAndre Lambert-Smith__, and __Brenen Thompson__ at the top of the WR depth chart, or if the team will sign Allen and slot him back in as the #3 WR. The Chargers let their young WRs get more reps in OTAs and minicamp last summer before signing Allen in the first week of August. Allen’s presence would be a major drag on the fantasy values of McConkey and company after he led the Chargers in TPRR (.26) at 33 years old. The additions of __Alec Ingold__, __Charlie Kolar__, and __David Njoku__ indicate that the Chargers are moving toward a heavier personnel approach under __Mike McDaniel__. There’s a decent chance Hortiz was just being respectful of a Chargers legend, which could create a small buying opportunity if McConkey’s fourth-round ADP (41, WR20) slips a bit. *(Added May 21)*

##### __Buffalo Bills__

+   __Dalton Kincaid__ has flashed elite TE traits early in his career, but he’s been a part-time player in Buffalo’s offense and has been unable to stay healthy. Better health could go a long way to increasing Kincaid’s opportunities in 2026, which would help him realize his full fantasy potential. He owns just a 57% route share in 42 of a possible 51 career games since the Bills selected him in the first round in 2023. Kincaid opted against surgery to fix a PCL injury he’s dealt with since 2014, electing to rehab the injury based on the recommendations of the doctors he talked to about his condition. He [said it’s the best he’s felt so far in his career](https://x.com/NickSabatoGNN/status/2056839766138569038?s=20), which was helped by adding 10-12 pounds of muscle this offseason. Kincaid led the league in TPRR (.27) and YPRR (3.19) among 53 TEs who ran 150+ routes, but he ranked seventh in route share (44.2%) among Bills receivers — he even ranked behind __Dawson Knox__ at 48.2%. I’ve been hoping that Kincaid could stay healthy and run more routes since he broke into the league, but it hasn’t happened yet heading into his fourth season. The Bills notably picked up his fifth-year option this spring, which is a sign that they could have bigger plans for him. It seems unlikely that __Joe Brady__ changes his approach at TE as he moves from offensive coordinator to head coach. It’s still worth taking a shot on Kincaid at his depressed ADP (131, TE13) because he has top-five potential at the position if he could ever get close to a 70% route share. *(Updated May 21)*

##### __Las Vegas Raiders__

+   ESPN’s Ryan McFadden believes the expectation is for __Kirk Cousins__ to open the season as the starting quarterback over first overall pick __Fernando Mendoza__. It’s not a big surprise, but Cousins received all of the first-team reps at early OTAs, while Mendoza worked mostly with rookies behind __Aidan O’Connell__. Mendoza will be watching from the sidelines in September if minority owner __Tom Brady__ has as much influence as it seems from the outside. Brady previously called it a “[tragedy](https://www.youtube.com/shorts/zyclRMckosM?sttick=0)” to force rookie quarterbacks to play early in their careers. The Raiders will pay $11.3 million guaranteed to Cousins to mentor Mendoza this season, which is a starter’s salary and makes him the 20th-highest-paid QB in average annual value. The bigger question is when Mendoza will enter the starting lineup. The Raiders don’t have any obvious on-ramps to get Mendoza in the lineup because all of their games are on Sunday, and their bye week doesn’t arrive until Week 13. Mendoza is off the radar in redraft leagues and a player to stash in 2-QB/Superflex formats to open the season. Cousins is a QB3 option for at least September in 2-QB/Superflex leagues. *(Added May 21)*

##### __Pittsburgh Steelers__

+   The Steelers and __Aaron Rodgers__ finally came to terms on a one-year, $22 million guaranteed deal that is worth up to $25 million. He said on May 20 that this upcoming season would be his last, but he admitted he thought 2025 would be his final season after __Mike Tomlin__ stepped away before being drawn back in by the Steelers' hiring __Mike McCarthy__. Rodgers wanted the ball out of his hands last season, finishing with the fastest average time to throw (2.38 seconds) and the fourth-lowest aDOT (6.3 yards) among 45 QBs who attempted 100+ passes. The style of play led him to rank 10th in catchable throw rate (76.9%) and fourth in turnover-worthy throw rate (1.6%), but 31st in hero throw rate (3.8%). He’s posted a solid 4.8% TD rate in each of his last three healthy campaigns, but he’s unlikely to do much better at 42 years old. The Steelers at least added __Michael Pittman__ and __Germie Bernard__ to a receiving corps that ranked 31st in 11 personnel (38.9%) under playcaller __Arthur Smith__. Rodgers will step into a familiar offense under his longtime Packers HC, whose offense ranked ninth in 11 personnel (70.8%) in his final season with the Cowboys. Rodgers won two of his four MVPs under McCarthy, but those days are long gone. He should at least have a little more upside than his QB27 (14.7) from last season, with a better receiving corps around him. *(Updated May 20)*

ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler [heard](https://x.com/ESPNCleveland/status/2056121255984566332?s=20) Watson has “hit it off with __Todd Monken,__” and Mary Kay Cabot [reported](https://x.com/MaryKayCabot/status/2049523640450871504?ref_src=twsrc%5Egoogle%7Ctwcamp%5Eserp%7Ctwgr%5Etweet) in late April that Watson took the lead over Sanders. The decision to go with Watson is also another indication that Monken’s offense could be more of a spread attack than his TE-heavy attack in Baltimore. The Browns already selected __KC Concepcion__ and __Denzel Boston__ inside the top 39 picks to bolster their WR depth, and Watson previously struggled in __Kevin Stefanski__’s under-center offense. Watson is entering the final year of his disastrous five-year, $230 million contract he signed in 2022, and the Browns clearly want to take one final look at Watson since they’re paying him so much money. The Browns can also ice the Shedeur hype early in the season, but he’ll eventually get opportunities to play later in the season once Watson flames out. *(Added May 19)*
